skill.name: database-architect
skill.description: Database architecture assistant for technology selection, schema modeling, index planning, migration strategy, and scalable data layer design.
skill.summary: Design data models, database choices, migrations, and scaling plans for new or changing systems.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 36 advises backups and rollback plans before destructive database changes. This is safe operational guidance, not system reconnaissance.
Line 43 describes designing the data layer early to avoid rework. It contains no instruction to inspect a host, enumerate files, or collect system details.
Line 60 discusses hybrid database architectures and synchronization as design options. This is architecture terminology, not reconnaissance or data collection.
Line 80 discusses hybrid normalization approaches like materialized views. It is normal database design content with no host inspection behavior.
Line 168 mentions hybrid cloud, private cloud, and data sovereignty as architecture considerations. It does not request network scanning or environment discovery.
Line 212 says backend services can be built on a solid data foundation. This is workflow positioning, not an instruction to examine the system.
Line 234 asks the assistant to generate ERD diagrams using Mermaid when requested. Diagram generation is documentation output, not system reconnaissance.
Line 245 is an example prompt for creating a healthcare appointment ERD. It does not ask for real patient data, environment access, or system enumeration.
Line 265 lists ERD diagrams using Mermaid as an output format. This is documentation capability, not reconnaissance behavior.

content.value_statement: Database choices and schemas are difficult to change after launch. This skill guides technology selection, schema modeling, migration planning, and scaling decisions.
actual_capabilities: Compares relational, NoSQL, time-series, graph, search, and cloud database options.
Designs conceptual, logical, and physical schemas with relationships, constraints, and data lifecycle policies.
Plans indexes, caching layers, partitioning, sharding, replication, and capacity strategies.
Creates migration strategies with validation, rollback planning, and zero-downtime rollout options.
Documents trade-offs, alternatives, and operational implications for database architecture decisions.
Generates Mermaid ERD diagrams when the user requests diagram output.
limitations: It recommends architecture and plans, but it does not execute migrations by default.
It is not focused on isolated query tuning without schema or architecture changes.
It needs workload, scale, consistency, and compliance requirements for strong recommendations.
It cannot verify live database performance without access to metrics or execution plans.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Product Data Layer
use_cases.description: Choose the right database model, schema shape, indexes, and scaling path before implementation begins.

use_cases.title: Modernize a Legacy Database
use_cases.description: Map migration phases, compatibility risks, rollback steps, and validation checks for a safer re-architecture.

use_cases.title: Design for Regulated Data
use_cases.description: Plan storage boundaries, access controls, retention, encryption, and audit patterns for sensitive data systems.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Database
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner technology selection for a new application.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose a database for a new application. The domain is [domain], expected users are [scale], and the main queries are [queries].

prompt_templates.title: Design a Schema
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate schema modeling for known entities and access patterns.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a schema for [system]. Include entities, relationships, constraints, indexes, and notes on normalization trade-offs.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Migration
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced migration planning for an existing production system.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a migration strategy from [current database] to [target database]. Include phases, validation, rollback, downtime risks, and operational checks.

prompt_templates.title: Architect for Scale
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced architecture design for high-volume or multi-region systems.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a scalable database architecture for [workload]. Include partitioning, sharding, replication, caching, consistency, disaster recovery, and monitoring.

output_examples.input: Design a database for a multi-tenant SaaS billing platform.
output: Recommends PostgreSQL with tenant-aware schema boundaries and row-level security.
Defines core entities such as accounts, subscriptions, invoices, payments, and audit events.
Adds indexes for tenant lookup, billing cycles, payment status, and reporting paths.
Includes migration phases, rollback checkpoints, and compliance notes.

output_examples.input: Plan a move from MongoDB to PostgreSQL for order data.
output: Compares document and relational trade-offs for order history and fulfillment workflows.
Proposes a relational model with orders, order items, customers, shipments, and status events.
Outlines parallel writes, backfill validation, cutover criteria, and rollback procedures.

output_examples.input: Create an architecture for IoT sensor events at high volume.
output: Recommends a time-series storage path with retention tiers and aggregation strategy.
Defines partitioning by device, time range, and ingestion volume.
Covers hot storage, cold storage, alert queries, and monitoring thresholds.

best_practices: Share access patterns, write volume, read volume, retention needs, and consistency expectations before asking for a design.
Ask for trade-offs between at least two database options when the technology choice is uncertain.
Request migration validation, rollback criteria, and monitoring plans for any production data change.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for a final schema without explaining the business entities and query patterns.
Do not use it only for small query tuning tasks that do not affect architecture.
Do not skip staging validation, backups, or rollback planning for destructive data changes.

faq.question: Can this skill choose between SQL and NoSQL databases?
faq.answer: Yes. It compares data shape, access patterns, consistency needs, scale, operations, and cost.

faq.question: Can it generate ERD diagrams?
faq.answer: Yes. It can produce Mermaid ERD diagrams when you request diagram output.

faq.question: Does it execute migrations automatically?
faq.answer: No. The skill focuses on migration planning and recommends execution only when explicitly requested.

faq.question: Is it useful for cloud database design?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers AWS, Azure, GCP, managed databases, multi-region design, and hybrid cloud considerations.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide domain entities, query patterns, scale targets, consistency needs, retention rules, and compliance constraints.

faq.question: How is it different from a database optimizer?
faq.answer: It focuses on architecture and data modeling, while optimizers focus on tuning existing queries and systems.
